human_tolerance.notes: The species article lists gardens among its habitats alongside coastal bush, open forest and fynbos, and describes it as common and conspicuous, perching at the top of a bush.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Nests mainly in the southern spring, September to November; the nest is a thick-walled cup concealed by foliage in a small tree or shrub.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Resident year-round and pairs hold foraging territory; the window covers the non-breeding part of the year.

vocalizations.description: A liquid whistle of two or more varied notes, transcribed in the source as 'pit-peet-pitmajol, piet-piet-patata', repeated from a perch.

external.note: GBIF usageKey 2486138 and iNaturalist taxon 14594 from the species/match and taxa endpoints; the Wikidata QID is the one the English article's taxobox links to.

conservation.note: The species article's taxobox records IUCN category Least Concern, credited there to BirdLife International.

range.note: 'An endemic resident breeder in coastal bush, open forest, gardens and fynbos in western and southern South Africa' gives ZA as the only native country; the range is not broken into provinces here because the stated area spans several. Koppen Csb is the Mediterranean warm-summer class the Western and Southern Cape winter-rainfall fynbos and garden habitats fall in.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: A perching passerine that forages in bush foliage and flies between perches; hop and fly are recorded from that description rather than stated as gaits.

traits.nest_type.note: 'The nest is a thick-walled cup concealed by foliage in a small tree or shrub.'

traits.perching.note: 'Tends to perch at the top of a bush.'

traits.mass_kg.note: AVONET Mass 38.6 g for Pycnonotus capensis, sourced by AVONET to Dunning.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Authored bracket of 32-45 g around the AVONET mean, for the modest size spread the single 38.6 g figure implies. No sourced range for this species was found; treat as an estimate, not a measurement.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Twice the AVONET Wing.Length of 92.8 mm, rounded to 0.186 m. AVONET does not give a wingspan directly.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Honest gap. Neither the species article, Wikidata nor GBIF gives a longevity figure for this species, and no openly licensed source with one was found. 6 years is an authored placeholder for a medium-small passerine; it is not a sourced value and a reviewer should replace it if a better source appears.

traits.diet.note: The article says the species forages 'for fruit, nectar and insects'. The 0.4/0.4/0.2 split between those three is authored, since the source gives no proportions.

traits.senses.note: Authored: diurnal passerine with coloured vision and modest olfaction.

traits.social.note: 'Usually seen in pairs or small groups'; the upper bound of 4 is authored.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Recorded as diurnal: a day-active garden and fynbos bird, with no nocturnal behaviour described.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement from 'a common and conspicuous bird' that habitually perches in gardens.

habitat.use.note: AVONET classifies the species' habitat as Shrubland with an insessorial lifestyle; the article adds gardens and open forest. The 0.7 arboreal / 0.3 ground split is authored from that.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Authored: roosts and nests in dense bush.

habitat.resources.note: Food tags follow the article's 'fruit, nectar and insects'; perch, shrub_thicket and the cup nest follow 'perch at the top of a bush' and the nest description. Weights are authored.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: The article lists gardens explicitly among the habitats, so uses_gardens is sourced; urban_affinity and light_max are authored.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'An endemic resident breeder', with no migration described.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding window September to November is stated; the non-breeding window as 'territorial' and its dates are authored.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Authored: a plain cup-nesting passerine with a nest_cup requirement for the egg stage and a fledging period of about two months.

vocalizations.song.note: The article gives the call and its transcription: 'a liquid whistle of two or more varied notes pit-peet-pitmajol, piet-piet-patata'.

look.note: Dull blackish-brown with a diagnostic white eye-ring, yellow undertail coverts, a small crest, and a short straight black bill and legs; proportions are authored.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: a bird that perches in bush, flies between perches and nests in a cup in a small tree or shrub in the southern spring. The program wants both a song and an alarm call, and the source documents only one call for this species, so the same documented whistle serves both contexts rather than a second call being invented.
